title: Ebola outbreak in eastern DR Congo

charter.in: The Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus that DR Congo declared on 15 May 2026 (WHO declared it a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May). It began in Ituri, spread through eastern, northern and northwestern provinces, and produced linked cases in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria and France. Stories belong when they report on the outbreak itself: its counts and spread, the response (treatment, tracing, vaccines and trials, funding appeals for it), setbacks such as strikes and attacks on responders, linked cases abroad, or people affected.
out: Global health funding cuts, USAID's dismantling and WHO budget stories that cite this outbreak only as an example
Pandemic preparedness reports, the WHO Pandemic Agreement (PABS annex) talks and UN pandemic declarations
Other outbreaks in the same places and months: cholera in DR Congo and Nigeria, polio, bird flu
The eastern Congo armed conflict and peace process (M23, AFC, MONUSCO) where it is not reported as hampering the Ebola response
Ebola vaccine or biosecurity research not tied to this outbreak
charter.endEvent: The Bundibugyo outbreak is declared over: DR Congo's health authorities and WHO declare it over, which is also the moment it is over in all affected countries, since Uganda's linked outbreak was declared over on 24 October 2026 and the other countries had only imported cases. Uganda's declaration alone, or any other country clearing its imported cases, does not end it.

figures.name: Cases
figures.definition: Confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases, cumulative since the outbreak was declared on 15 May 2026, all affected countries; nearly all are in DR Congo, so a DR Congo total and an all-country total both match. Most of our stories say 'confirmed cases'; stories that say 'cases', 'reported cases', 'recorded cases' or 'people infected' give the same running tally and also match. Not counted: suspected cases, early totals that include suspected cases, and counts for one country other than DR Congo, one place, or health workers only.
variants: suspected cases (246 on 17 May, nearly 750 on 23 May, nearly 1,000 on 29 May)
early total including suspected cases (over 500 by 19 May)
one country other than DR Congo (Uganda: 2, 7, 19, 20; Kenya: 9)
DR Congo government count quoted by CIDRAP on 2 November (6,100), far below the running total

figures.name: Deaths
figures.definition: Deaths among confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases, cumulative since the outbreak was declared on 15 May 2026, all affected countries (nearly all in DR Congo), as WHO, Africa CDC, the UN or DR Congo report them. Not counted: suspected deaths, early totals that include suspected deaths, deaths in one place or one reporting window, and health-worker deaths only.
variants: suspected deaths (about 80 on 17 May, over 220 on 29 May)
early total including suspected deaths (130 by 19 May)
one place (Kigonze camp, Beni health zone)
deaths reported since a date (512 since 21 October)
DR Congo government count quoted by CIDRAP on 2 November (2,950), far below the running total
UN 'more than 5,000' and Africa CDC 'more than 5,400' in mid-November: the same count, rounded differently

responses.what: WHO declaring a public health emergency of international concern for the Bundibugyo outbreak.
responses.quote: WHO has declared a PHEIC for Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus after confirmed cases in Ituri province (DRC) and cases in Kampala and Kinshasa.

responses.what: UN agencies mobilizing staff, $60 million and supplies for the outbreak response.
responses.quote: UN agencies mobilized staff, $60 million and supplies; two cases reached Uganda.

responses.what: WHO placing the outbreak under a global public health emergency declaration.
responses.quote: An Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC was declared a global public health emergency on 17 May 2026 after rapid case growth: over 500 cases and 130 deaths by 19 May.

responses.what: Uganda closing its border to contain cross-border Ebola transmission.
responses.quote: Uganda closed its border and WHO escalated cross-border surveillance as regional health systems strain under the combined crises.

responses.what: The US imposing entry bans in response to the outbreak.
responses.quote: The US is urging travel restrictions and has imposed entry bans, which raises the profile of the outbreak and affects travel and event planning during the World Cup.

responses.what: Ebola response teams following up known contacts in northeastern DR Congo, despite severely limited coverage.
responses.quote: For example, only 28.4% of known contacts were followed up on June 11, allowing chains of transmission to continue.

responses.what: WHO and international teams mobilizing assistance for the outbreak.
responses.quote: Poor sanitation, crowded displacement camps, and cuts to WASH funding are hampering the response while WHO and international teams rush to help.

responses.what: Neighboring states using border and airport closures to restrict movement during the outbreak.
responses.quote: Neighbouring states have used unilateral border and airport closures instead of coordinated WHO-guided responses, which undermines joint action across DRC, Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.

responses.what: Bundibugyo treatment-trial teams beginning participant enrollment.
responses.quote: The outbreak has recorded 1,708 cases and 580 deaths, treatment centers are near capacity, and clinical trial enrollment for a Bundibugyo treatment has just begun.

responses.what: Post-exposure prophylaxis trial teams recruiting roughly 1,000 contacts in Ituri.
responses.quote: A post-exposure prophylaxis trial has begun recruiting roughly 1,000 contacts in Ituri, offering a potential tool to prevent infections if results are positive.

responses.what: WHO maintaining the outbreak under an international public health emergency declaration.
responses.quote: The virus is spreading faster than response teams can contain it, health services are strained, and WHO has declared an international public health emergency.

responses.what: The WHO-sponsored PARTNERS trial beginning to test treatment options for Bundibugyo.
responses.quote: That scientific gap means care is limited to supportive treatment while the WHO-sponsored PARTNERS trial only now begins to test options.

responses.what: Rapid-response teams carrying out safe burials and clinical case management in affected towns.
responses.quote: Rapid response teams, safe and dignified burials, and clinical case management have produced local stabilization in places like Mongbwalu and parts of Goma, showing that focused measures can slow transmission.

responses.what: Oxford Vaccine Group starting a rapid experimental vaccine trial.
responses.quote: Oxford Vaccine Group has started a rapid experimental trial, but that is an early step with uncertain timelines and coverage.

responses.what: Experimental Bundibugyo vaccine trial teams beginning first-dose trials.
responses.quote: The experimental Bundibugyo vaccine has started first-dose trials, but remains preliminary and will not mitigate near-term risk until proven effective and widely deployed.

responses.what: Clinical-trial teams running two post-exposure drug trials for the outbreak.
responses.quote: Two post-exposure drug trials and vaccine trials abroad have started, but they are experimental and will take time to change outcomes.

responses.what: Gavi making stockpiled Ervebo doses available for trials against Bundibugyo.
responses.quote: Gavi holds a 500,000-dose Ervebo stockpile and has made doses available for trials, creating a concrete, near-term path to test whether an existing vaccine can be reused.

responses.what: DR Congo authorities scaling up treatment and monitoring.
responses.quote: Cases have spread from one health zone to 54 across six provinces, and insecurity and population movement are complicating surveillance and response while authorities scale up treatment and monitoring.

responses.what: WHO recruiting motorbike riders for community Ebola surveillance.
responses.quote: WHO is scaling up community engagement, recruiting motorbike riders for surveillance, adding beds, and deploying hundreds of health workers, while facing community resistance and attacks on responders.

responses.what: WHO releasing 70,000 Ervebo doses for a trial and frontline-worker vaccination.
responses.quote: The WHO has allocated 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine — 20,000 for a late-stage trial and 50,000 for health workers — while Gavi pledged $13m to support shipment and vaccination efforts amid a declared global emergency.

responses.quote: The US provided $80 million but that does not close the gap.

notes:
FIGURES. Cases are confirmed cases, the wording of most of our stories (32 of the 49 entries with a matching case count). The other stories write 'cases', 'reported cases', 'recorded cases' or 'people infected', but their numbers sit on the same running tally (e.g. 5,290 'infected' on 22 Aug between 5,208 and 5,794 confirmed on 21 and 29 Aug), so they match. Marked false: suspected counts (17 to 29 May), the WHO total of over 500 cases and 130 deaths by 19 May (our text does not say suspected, but 82 cases and 7 deaths were confirmed on 23 May, so it must include suspected ones), counts for Uganda or Kenya alone, one place (Kigonze camp, Beni), health workers only, and deaths since 21 October. A DR Congo-only total and an all-country total both match, since other countries add only a few dozen cases.

NARROWER OR STALE COUNTS. 2 Nov (CIDRAP): 2,950 deaths among 6,100 cases, 'latest government numbers', against more than 10,400 cases and 5,103 deaths by 31 Oct (11 Nov story) and 5,126 by 1 Nov (7 Nov story). Our text does not say why, so both values are matches false and asOf is the story date. 16 Oct (Lancet): its title gives 2,788 deaths when the toll was over 4,000, but the text dates the count to 26 Aug, so asOf is 26 Aug and it matches. 22 Jul: the Sudan roundup's 2,344 cases and 930 deaths are lower than the 2,423 and 967 as of 19 Jul in the same day's UN story.

MID-NOVEMBER DEATHS. The 14 Nov story itself flags that the UN said 'more than 5,000' while Africa CDC said 'more than 5,400' as of 12 Nov. The 16 Nov story's confirmed count of 5,433 as of 12 Nov supports Africa CDC: the UN figure is a loose floor rather than a different definition, so both match. Also notable: 5,376 deaths on 3 Nov (Al Jazeera) is about 250 above the UN's 5,126 by 1 Nov, and 'over 5,300' on 7 Nov sits beside 5,126 in the same-day UN story. No definitions are given, so all of them match.

COUNTRIES. Kenya: the 7 Oct story reports its first confirmed case (a traveler who died in Nairobi), 11 and 24 Oct repeat it, 28 Oct says 'Kenya reported nine cases', and 3 Nov says 'Kenya recorded its first cases'. The 3 Nov wording contradicts the earlier stories, and the status row keeps it as worded. Nigeria: the 22 Oct story reports its first confirmed case (travel from Uganda), 30 Oct repeats one imported case, 1 Nov reports two suspected cases isolated, and 3 Nov says the suspected cases tested negative. The negative tests concern the two suspected cases only, not the confirmed October case. Yet the 3 Nov title counts 'three countries' (DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya), leaving out Nigeria and France, where the 30 Oct Africa CDC story counted five countries. France's imported case is first reported on 16 Aug. Uganda: cases from 17 May, no new cases by 3 Jul, outbreak declared over in the 24 Oct story. That is a status inside this development, not its end, so closed stays null: no story reports DR Congo's outbreak declared over.

OTHER INCONSISTENCIES. The 25 May title says 'Goma cases surge past 500', but the text counts all of DR Congo. The 17 May story says 'eight lab-confirmed cases' in its summary and antifactors, but its reasons say 'eight in Ituri, plus cases in Kinshasa and Kampala'. The key reads eight as the total. The 6 Sep African Arguments piece says Africa's systems 'are containing spread' while same-week stories report more than 3,000 deaths and uncontrolled spread.

CONVENTIONS. Quotes come only from title, summary, relevance reasons, antifactors and research paragraphs. When a story states one number both rounded and exact, the key lists the exact one. In 'more than X cases and Y deaths', the qualifier also applies to Y when Y is a round number (2,700, 4,000). Single-case country firsts are statuses, not values. Weekly incidence ('400 to 500 a week') is not recorded. Optional joins: two roundups that give Ebola one paragraph (3 Jul, 22 Jul) and two essays that use the outbreak as the opening case for a wider argument (6 Sep, 19 Sep). Of the two 7 Nov stories on the same vaccine decision, both are turning points because they were published at the same time. The 2 Nov CIDRAP quick take is a must because the outbreak is its lead item and title.

END EVENT. Since 2026-11-22 (the owner's decision) the end event says that DR Congo's declaration and the outbreak declared over in all affected countries are one event, since Uganda's was declared over on 24 Oct and the other countries had only imported cases: the end-event judge read a founding that named all affected countries as a wider event than DR Congo's declaration.

ROLES. Entries with `eitherRole` accept either verdict; each says why in `roleReview` (an AI session's review of 2026-11-22, not yet checked by a person). The count updates the linking eval called setbacks or spread (deaths passing 3,000, 61 health zones, the Lancet comments with stale counts) stay routine.
